overview: Use case: stylized-concept. Create one high quality architectural game environment concept presentation of an old modest Korean goshiwon called Haedam. This is a design preview, NOT an existing gameplay screenshot. Landscape 3:2 composition. Show a single long narrow THREE STOREY building plus an open ROOFTOP as four vertically exploded horizontal cutaway slabs, offset only slightly, each clearly visible, aligned in the same footprint. View at elevated isometric angle, remove ceilings and front walls for visibility. Reference image 1 is the authoritative SECOND AND THIRD FLOOR spatial/material reference. Reference image 2 is the ROOFTOP plan. Reference image 3 is the FIRST FLOOR plan (different communal layout). Preserve their topology. Each inhabited floor has twelve tiny rooms in a single straight row along the back exterior window wall, all facing ONE narrow 1.3m corridor. Small rooms about 2.3m wide x3m deep and low 2.6m ceilings. NO second parallel corridor, no hotel lobby, no oversized bedrooms. Widened open corridor ends with exterior walls retained. Interior return staircase at RIGHT extremity links all three floors and rooftop in same vertical shaft; exterior rusty fire escape LEFT. First floor far LEFT entrance has a TINY caretaker office with a solid half-height lower wall and glazed upper wall facing entrance, and SIDE door, with only desk/chair and narrow sleeping clearance. First floor front communal strip from left to right: tiny office/storage, compact kitchen two round tables, toilets with sinks, independent larger shower room, right stairs. Second and third floor front communal strip: storage left, enlarged communal kitchen with exactly TWO ROUND wooden dining tables and ordinary chairs, kitchen countertop and refrigerator against exterior wall opposite corridor doorway; separate shower room next, separate toilet room (sinks left toilet cubicles right), stairs far right. Keep every doorway clear. No lounge on any floor. Only five rooms per floor furnished/lived in; other rooms sparse or empty, 202 and307 have bare bed frames and desks only. No people, no monsters. Rooftop green weathered waterproof coating, waist-high parapet, right stairhead and sheltered laundry corner, central lines of hanging white sheets leaving a walking route, water tank/service corner left. Respect the long rectangular footprint, do not invent another residential floor. Materials from reference: yellowed cracked wallpaper, dull green patterned corridor vinyl, aged timber doors, beige kitchen tiles, gray bathroom tiles, fluorescent fixtures, mild moisture staining, lived-in and old but not demolished. Readable neutral studio lighting with subtle nighttime blue, dark charcoal background. Architectural clarity over cinematic darkness. Only small labels at LEFT of each slab: '옥상', '3층', '2층', '1층'. Elegant small heading '해담고시원 · 건물 구성 시안'. Do not add diagram arrows, dimensions, other text or glowing game markers. Produce an attractive believable realistic 3D concept render, accurate to narrow cheap goshiwon character.

This is a concept rendering, not exact construction or game capture.
kit:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create ONE unified architectural modular-kit concept contact sheet for the aged Korean goshiwon horror game. This is an IMAGE PREVIEW BEFORE 3D GENERATION. Landscape 3:2 high resolution. Exactly TEN numbered panels in a clean 5-column by 2-row grid, equal size, generous gutter, muted light gray studio background. Consistent realistic 3D environment asset rendering, 3/4 isometric view, neutral readable soft light. Reference image is MATERIAL and STYLE only: faded cream wallpaper, dull green patterned vinyl flooring, dark old timber trims, beige tiles, moisture and age, sensible construction. Each panel is a DIFFERENT BUILDING COMPONENT not a furnished room diorama. No people or monsters. No tiny props, chairs, appliances or table. No text apart from the exact labels below and header '해담고시원 · 건축 모듈 10종 시안'. Do not merge assets across panels.
TOP ROW:
'01 복도 벽' — narrow old wallpapered wall bay, timber skirting and OPEN EMPTY rectangular door frame, no door leaf, straight regular edges for tiling.
'02 창문 외벽' — exterior wall bay with modest rectangular aluminum window opening and sill, aged concrete outside and wallpaper inside, glass pane omitted.
'03 객실 골조' — tiny empty room shell about 2.3x3 meters: floor plus back wall with small window plus two side walls, no ceiling, open front, zero furnishings, dark timber floor skirting.
'04 관리실 전면' — small L-shaped enclosure front is solid half-height lower wall with upper glazed frame, RETURN SIDE wall has EMPTY SIDE DOOR opening, no door leaf, no desk, no furnishings; miniature office not a shop.
'05 주방 골조' — beige tiled floor with a back wall and single side wall, weathered backsplash tile, small exterior window, EMPTY unfurnished shell, no counter or objects.
BOTTOM ROW:
'06 화장실 칸막이' — two gray-tiled toilet cubicle partition bays with door frames, open empty inside, no toilet bowls, no shower, no door leaves, separable looking straight panels.
'07 샤워실 칸막이' — two privacy shower partition bays of frosted metal framed panels with tiled floor and drains, EMPTY front openings with no door leaves, no people, no toilet, simple straight panels.
'08 실내 계단' — COMPACT CONCRETE U-RETURN STAIR, TWO PARALLEL FLIGHTS connected by a half-height LANDING at back, simple steel center railing, first flight rises away from camera and second returns upward toward camera, clearly stair geometry, no walls obscuring it.
'09 외부 비상계단' — one storey worn dark galvanized metal fire escape assembly, two flights and landing with safety rails, repeatable vertically, isolated and complete.
'10 옥상 난간' — L-shaped weathered concrete rooftop parapet corner with green waterproof floor edging, low waist-high wall with coping, EMPTY no tank no laundry poles.
No visual part should obscure openings. Parts are mesh concept references to be measured and separated in Blender later, do not present furnished architecture or an entire building. Every part clearly isolated. Maintain shabby modest believable Korean low-budget accommodation rather than dungeon/gothic/hotel. The ten numbered labels must match the parts and appear beneath each object.
kitCorrection: Precisely edit ONLY panel '08 실내 계단' in this existing 10-panel architecture contact sheet. Leave all other nine panels, all labels, overall canvas layout and header unchanged. REPLACE the incorrect side-by-side straight flights with a realistic buildable concrete SWITCHBACK U-SHAPED STAIR ASSEMBLY serving one storey. Two parallel stair flights at DIFFERENT HEIGHTS: left lower flight starts at bottom-front and goes UP AWAY from camera to a MID-LEVEL LANDING at the far rear; right UPPER flight starts on that same mid-level rear landing and ascends BACK TOWARD the camera, ending on a HIGH FRONT-RIGHT TOP LANDING, approximately 3.2 meters above bottom start. Thus the near-right end is visibly HIGH while near-left start is LOW. Show the upper flight underside and void beneath it, supported by concrete slab, with metal handrails. Use a slightly rotated side isometric angle within this cell so the U-turn and vertically stacked walking path are unmistakable. Do NOT place both stair bottoms at same front height. Do NOT make two side-by-side stairs going in same direction. This should look like a normal dogleg staircase with two opposite-direction flights, not a twin escalator. Exposed standalone assembly without enclosing walls, worn gray concrete steps and dull metal railings, matching rest of kit. Keep exact label '08 실내 계단'.
